name: The Jan Dzierzon Oak

location.address: Bulwar on the Odra Canal embankment, ul. Bartla, Wroclaw
location.neighbourhood: Szczytniki, on the riverside path between the Zwierzyniecki and Szczytnicki bridges

verified_sources: https://przyrodniczo.pl/pomniki-przyrody/pomniki-przyrody-wielka-wyspa/ (dedicated survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees, with current measurements and health notes)
access: Free, on the public riverside boulevard/embankment along the Oder canal, open at all times
transport: Tram stops serving Most Zwierzyniecki, about 10 minutes' walk along the river path
verify_notes: Registered as a Polish pomnik przyrody (nature monument), decision 5/53, 16 Feb 1953. Girth 652cm, height 22m per przyrodniczo.pl's dedicated 2020s survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees (independent of the GDOS register, which carries no girth/height field at all), corroborated for species, coordinates and designation date by the GDOS CRFOP register. Known until 1945 as the Hobrecht-Eiche (Hobrecht Oak), after Breslau's mayor Artur Hobrecht, who in 1865 bought the riverside plot on the city's behalf specifically to keep the tree standing. Renamed after Polish annexation for Jan Dzierzon, the beekeeping pioneer. Its interior is now significantly decayed (hollow, poor structural condition per the 2020s survey) but the tree is alive and in leaf. Part of a walkable cluster of four named oaks on Wroclaw's Wielka Wyspa (Great Island), all within 1.3km of each other, three of them century-old monuments from the same 1953 designation batch.

name: The Dziadek Oak

location.address: ul. Mikolaja Kopernika, in front of the State Labour Inspectorate training centre, Wroclaw
location.neighbourhood: Dabie, on the edge of Park Szczytnicki

verified_sources: https://przyrodniczo.pl/pomniki-przyrody/pomniki-przyrody-wielka-wyspa/ (dedicated survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees, with current measurements and health notes)
access: Free; the tree stands on the public street/pavement in front of the training centre building, not inside its grounds
transport: Tram/bus stops on ul. Kopernika, a few minutes' walk from Park Szczytnicki
verify_notes: Registered as a Polish pomnik przyrody (nature monument), decision 2/53, 16 Feb 1953. Girth 652.5cm, height 17m per przyrodniczo.pl's dedicated 2020s survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees (independent of the GDOS register, which carries no girth/height field at all), corroborated for species, coordinates and designation date by the GDOS CRFOP register. Reported as the oldest tree in Wroclaw. Its name means 'Grandpa' in Polish. The trunk carries serious damage and the tree is kept alive with elastic bindings and steel clamps reinforcing its branches; still alive and monitored, per multiple recent surveys (629cm girth in 2015, 652.5cm in 2019). Part of a walkable cluster of four named oaks on Wroclaw's Wielka Wyspa (Great Island), all within 1.3km of each other, three of them century-old monuments from the same 1953 designation batch.

name: The Piotr Wlast Oak

location.neighbourhood: Dabie, near Park Szczytnicki and the Wroclaw Zoo

verified_sources: https://przyrodniczo.pl/pomniki-przyrody/pomniki-przyrody-wielka-wyspa/ (dedicated survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees, with current measurements and health notes)
transport: Bus/tram stops near the Wroclaw Zoo entrance on ul. Wroblewskiego, a few minutes' walk
verify_notes: Registered as a Polish pomnik przyrody (nature monument), decision 3/53, 16 Feb 1953. Girth 510cm, height 25m per przyrodniczo.pl's dedicated 2020s survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees (independent of the GDOS register, which carries no girth/height field at all), corroborated for species, coordinates and designation date by the GDOS CRFOP register. A solitary oak with a large, well-formed crown, in good health per the most recent survey, unlike its more storm-battered neighbours in this cluster. Named for Piotr Wlostowic (Piotr Wlast), a powerful 12th-century Polish magnate and monastery founder connected to the Wroclaw area; the naming is a historical dedication rather than a claim that the tree itself dates to his lifetime, and no independent age estimate for the tree itself was found this pass. Part of a walkable cluster of four named oaks on Wroclaw's Wielka Wyspa (Great Island), all within 1.3km of each other, three of them century-old monuments from the same 1953 designation batch.

verified_sources: https://przyrodniczo.pl/pomniki-przyrody/pomniki-przyrody-wielka-wyspa/ (dedicated survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees, with current measurements and health notes)

verify_notes: Registered as a Polish pomnik przyrody (nature monument), decision 26/76, 2 Apr 1976. Girth 554cm, height 26m per przyrodniczo.pl's dedicated 2020s survey of Wielka Wyspa's monument trees (independent of the GDOS register, which carries no girth/height field at all), corroborated for species, coordinates and designation date by the GDOS CRFOP register. Stands inside Park Szczytnicki, Wroclaw's large historic park beside the UNESCO-listed Centennial Hall. Damaged by a lightning strike, which has left it in poor structural condition, but it is alive and still in leaf; no independently sourced age estimate was found this pass beyond the register's 1976 designation date. Part of a walkable cluster of four named oaks on Wroclaw's Wielka Wyspa (Great Island), all within 1.3km of each other, three of them century-old monuments from the same 1953 designation batch.
